How far each starting point moved the pick from the best-scoring rule

Source: R/tune_anchor.R
knw_tune_anchor.Rd

The pick is the one-SE region's rule with the fewest departures from a starting point (knw_tune_score()), so where the data cannot rank several rules apart, the start chooses between them. This sets the two picks a tuning table holds beside the rule the data score best, and counts how far apart they are, so how much a baseline steered a published rule is a number rather than a reading (#141, #139).

Usage

knw_tune_anchor(tune, d_floor = formals(knw_tune_score)$d_floor)

Arguments

tune

a tuning table as knw_tune_score() returns it or scripts/0320 saves it (<sp>_<stage>_tune.csv, read as text or typed): rule, size_var, size_min, grad_max, exc_q, exc_d, in_region, recommended, ddev_best and se_diff; and departures_flow with recommended_flow where the table has a flow start (a table from before #80, or a species with no flow start, has none).

d_floor

numeric(1) the shortest exception distance (m) a pick may carry; knw_tune_score()'s own by default, so the register's one value (inst/method/settings.csv) holds for both.

Value

One row: rule_recommended, recommended_ddev and recommended_se (the pick from default, its distance behind the best and that distance's SE); the same for the flow start (rule_recommended_flow, recommended_flow_ddev, recommended_flow_se; NA with no flow start); rule_best and best_n; rule_best_allowed, best_allowed_ddev and best_is_allowed; rec_moved and flow_moved (each pick's departures from the best, 0 to 3), rec_moved_allowed and flow_moved_allowed (from the best allowed) and starts_apart (between the two picks), each with its parts (rec_moved_parts and so on: size, gradient and exception joined by +, or none); rec_is_best, flow_is_best (the pick is tied at the best) and starts_agree.

Details

The picks are the recommended rules, the ones published: from link's default (recommended) and from its flow version (recommended_flow, #80). The best is every rule at ddev_best == 0: rules with the same in/out on every visit are one fit and tie, so rule_best is the first of them in grid order (as scripts/0320's summary names it), best_n counts them, and a pick's distance to the best is its fewest departures from any of them, the first such rule in grid order naming the parts. Two rules depart in the three parts the grid counts (knw_tune_grid()): the size test (its variable or floor), the gradient maximum and the exception (its river size or distance, or one having it and the other not).

No pick may carry an exception closer than d_floor, but the best may, and then no start could reach it: part of the distance is the floor's, not the start's. So each pick is also measured against the best allowed rule, the best-scoring rule a pick may be: the lowest-scoring rule in the region (which holds converged rules only) with no exception or one at d_floor or more (ties as above). It is the best itself wherever best_is_allowed; the best is not allowed when its exception is under the floor, or when it did not converge (the best is the lowest score over every rule).

Examples

tune <- data.frame(
  rule = c("width>=1.5|g<=0.0549|none", "width>=2|g<=0.0549|none", "mad>=0.5|g<=0.0549|none",
           "width>=1|g<=0.0549|Q50@D500"),
  size_var = c("width", "width", "mad", "width"), size_min = c(1.5, 2, 0.5, 1), grad_max = 0.0549,
  exc_q = c(NA, NA, NA, 50), exc_d = c(NA, NA, NA, 500),
  departures_flow = c(1L, 1L, 0L, 2L), in_region = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE),
  recommended = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE), recommended_flow = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE),
  ddev_best = c(20, 5.7, 11.6, 0), se_diff = c(9, 10.4, 13.9, 0)
)
# from default the pick is two parts from the best (its width floor and the exception),
# and the flow start picks another rule, one part from it
knw_tune_anchor(tune)[, c("rule_recommended", "rec_moved", "rec_moved_parts", "rule_recommended_flow",
                          "starts_apart", "starts_apart_parts")]
#>          rule_recommended rec_moved rec_moved_parts   rule_recommended_flow
#> 1 width>=2|g<=0.0549|none         2  size+exception mad>=0.5|g<=0.0549|none
#>   starts_apart starts_apart_parts
#> 1            1               size
